qsm-uix screenshot.description: Capture one full monitor to a PNG; without --output the focused monitor is used

args.name: out
args.description: file to write (default: a timestamped file under the kit's output directory)

qsm-uix crop.description: Cut a region out of an image and magnify it with a point filter, so edges and antialiasing stay honest

args.name: out
args.description: file to write (default: a timestamped file under the kit's output directory)

qsm-uix diff.description: Compare two captures and report the SSIM distortion, where 0 means identical, plus a difference image

args.name: out
args.description: difference image to write (default: a timestamped file under the kit's output directory)

qsm-uix burst.description: Take a timed sequence of monitor frames and report each frame's real elapsed time, for judging motion

args.name: outDir
args.description: directory the frames are written into

qsm-uix pixel-sample.description: Read one pixel of an image as hex, OKLCH and rgb, so a colour claim cites the rendered pixel and not the name in code

qsm-uix contrast.description: WCAG contrast ratio between two pixels of an image, with the AA verdicts for body text and for large text or an essential glyph

qsm-uix region-stats.description: Colour and brightness statistics of a region: pixel count, distinct colours, mean luminance, the brightest and darkest pixel, and the dominant palette with each colour's share and OKLCH

args.name: rect
args.description: region as X,Y,W,H, at most 65536 pixels

args.name: top
args.description: how many palette entries to report (default 6)

qsm-uix a11y-tree.description: Print the platform accessibility tree (AT-SPI): per node indent, role, name, and the focused, focusable and showing states; filtered to one application when named

args.name: app
args.description: application name, or part of it (default: every application on the bus)

args.name: depth
args.description: levels below each application to walk (default 32)

qsm-uix doctor.description: Report whether the screenshot, image and key-sender tools are on PATH and the AT-SPI bus answers, naming the remedy for each one that does not
